title: Strict extension of edge-inverting diagrams along Kan anodyne maps
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, equivalence edges, full functor categories and Kan complexes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Call a map Kan anodyne if it belongs to the closure of all horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, under isomorphisms, pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts. For a simplicial set $K$ and quasicategory $E$, let $H(K,E)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ whose objects send every edge of $K$ to an equivalence; parameter directions are unrestricted. If $i:K\hookrightarrow K'$ is Kan anodyne, restriction
$$H(K',E)\longrightarrow H(K,E)$$
has the right lifting property against every simplicial boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq0$; thus it is a trivial Kan fibration. This assertion includes strict extensions with arbitrary already specified parameter-boundary data, not just an equivalence of functor categories. The construction is compatible with restriction in the parameter and postcomposition in $E$.

source.place: Corollary 3.5.13 with terminal target (all-edge-inverting exponential restriction and strict boundary lifting) Online source read on 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: For every small simplicial set $P$, put $G(P,E)=\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)^\simeq$, the core. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], applied to the quasicategory $E$ and the shape $P$, an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)$ is an equivalence exactly when each component at a vertex of $P$ is an equivalence edge of $E$. (No quasicategory property of $\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)$ or $H(K,E)$ is needed here; the core is the simplicial subset of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].) The degreewise functor-category definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives the interchange bijection between maps $P\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ and maps $K\to\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)$, both represented by a map $P\times K\to E$. The first factors through $H(K,E)$ precisely when every edge of $K$ maps to an equivalence at every vertex of $P$: by the definition of full subcategory it suffices and is necessary to test its vertices. By the cited componentwise criterion this is precisely the condition that every edge of $K$ maps to an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)$. The core definition then says exactly that the transposed map factors through $G(P,E)$. We obtain a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(P,H(K,E))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,G(P,E))$. This imposes no equivalence condition on the parameter edges of $P$.

source.place: Section 3.5.7, equation (3.5.7.2), and Corollary 3.5.12: interchange and the componentwise equivalence criterion.

proof.text: Fix $m\geq0$ and put $b_m:P=\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow Q=\Delta^m$, where the boundary is the union of the proper faces and $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. This is degreewise injective. The particular-case assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] makes restriction $r_m:\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(P,E)$ an isofibration between quasicategories, for every quasicategory $E$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration] to this isofibration. It gives a Kan fibration $q_m=r_m^\simeq:G(Q,E)\to G(P,E)$, that is, a map with the right lifting property against every horn, including both outer horns. This applies also when $m=0$, since the exponentiation assertion allows the empty subcomplex.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.11 with terminal target and Corollary 3.5.12; exponentiation restriction and passage to cores.

proof.text: Consider any boundary lifting square with top $a:P\to H(K',E)$ and bottom $b:Q\to H(K,E)$, so that restriction along $i$ gives $r_i a=b|_P$, where $r_i:H(K',E)\to H(K,E)$ is the restriction map. Step 1 transposes it to a square with top $\widetilde b:K\to G(Q,E)$, left map $i:K\hookrightarrow K'$, bottom $\widetilde a:K'\to G(P,E)$ and right map $q_m$. The original square commutes if and only if $q_m\widetilde b=\widetilde a i$: both equations assert equality of the same map $K\times P\to E$. A diagonal $K'\to G(Q,E)$ transposes back to a map $Q\to H(K',E)$. Its two triangle equalities state exactly that it restricts to $a$ on $P$ and to $b$ on $K$. Thus the correspondence is a bijection on fillers and preserves the boundary data strictly, by the degreewise formulas of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Corollary 3.5.13, displayed correspondence of lifting problems with terminal target; the two transpose equations are expanded here.

proof.text: For the fixed Kan fibration $q_m$ of Step 2, let $L_m$ be the class of maps having the left lifting property against $q_m$. By the definition in [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration], every horn inclusion is in $L_m$. Here is the elementary closure argument: isomorphisms lift by taking their inverses; a square for a pushout restricts to one for the attached map, whose filler glues with the given map on the old summand by the pushout universal property. For a small continuous transfinite composition, start with the prescribed map on its source, choose an extension at each successor using that stage's lifting property and the fixed bottom map restricted to that stage, and use the compatible colimit map at each limit. Every triangle equality holds at each stage and hence on the colimit. For a retract in the arrow category, precompose the top of the square by the domain retraction and the bottom by the codomain retraction, lift for the larger arrow, and precompose the resulting diagonal by the codomain section. The retract equations give both required triangle equalities. Consequently $L_m$ contains the closure of the horns under exactly the operations defining Kan anodyne in the item. Thus $i$ lifts against $q_m$ for every $m\geq0$, and Step 3 yields every required boundary filler for $H(K',E)\to H(K,E)$.

source.place: Corollary 3.5.13, conclusion from Theorem 3.5.11; the weak-saturation lifting argument is written out explicitly.

proof.text: A simplicial map $u:E\to F$ between quasicategories preserves equivalences by sending the inverse-triangle witnesses of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] to the corresponding witnesses in $F$. For any parameter map $v:P'\to P$, precomposition and postcomposition send the underlying map $h:P\times K\to E$ to the single composite $u\circ h\circ(v\times\mathrm{id}_K)$. This is the same composite whichever order the operations and the transposition take. Hence the restriction maps, the correspondence of lifting problems, and the sets of their fillers have the claimed compatibility with parameter restriction and postcomposition. Finally $m=0$ in Step 4 gives strict extension on objects, and all higher $m$ give arbitrary prescribed parameter-boundary data. The right lifting property against these boundaries is precisely the stated trivial Kan fibration convention.

source.place: Section 3.5.7 and Corollary 3.5.13: naturality of the exponential interchange and strict-lifting conclusion.
